Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NovaVolt Automotive Q4 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. There will be an opportunity to ask a question after the presentation. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to NovaVolt Automotive's Q4 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Jordan Hale, CEO; Sarah Chen, CFO; Mike Thornton, Chief Manufacturing Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jordan Hale.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Q4 2024 was a strong quarter for NovaVolt Automotive. We made significant progress in several key areas, including our strategic outlook and priorities for the coming year, raw material sourcing and cost management, delivery volume guidance by model, gross margin per vehicle performance, and total revenue with robust year-over-year growth. The demand for our NVX SUV continues to be strong, and we are working diligently to increase production capacity to meet that demand. The impact of this product lineup is exceeding our initial expectations, driving market share gains in the premium EV segment.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Jordan. Good morning, everyone. For Q4 2024, our total revenue reached $25.3 billion, representing a 42% increase year-over-year from $17.8 billion in the prior year period. This marks another record quarter and underscores the strength of our EV ecosystem and execution across our vertical integration strategy. Breaking it down by segment, automotive revenue, which accounted for 87% of the total at $22 billion, surged 51% year-over-year. This was propelled by record vehicle deliveries of 502,000 units—up 62% from 310,000 units last year—fueled by ramps in our NVX platform, the NVX SUV, and refreshed compact models. Average selling price held steady at $48,500 per vehicle, up 4% year-over-year, thanks to a richer mix with higher-margin long-range variants and performance trims. Regulatory credit sales added $950 million, up 15% year-over-year, as we capitalized on excess ZEV credits from slower ICE transitions by legacy OEMs.

Energy generation and storage revenue hit $2.5 billion, a 28% year-over-year increase, driven by deployments of our 4680 cell-based PowerWall equivalents and Megapack-scale installations. We shipped 12.5 GWh of energy storage in the quarter, with deployments accelerating in Texas, California grid projects, and Europe, where our LFP-NMC hybrid packs are outperforming on cycle life. Services and other revenue grew 35% to $800 million, benefiting from our expanding Supercharger rival network—now at 15,000 stalls globally—and over-the-air software updates, including our ADAS suite, which saw 65% fleet adoption and generated $350 million in premium feature unlocks.

Regionally, North America contributed 62% of revenue at $15.7 billion, up 55% year-over-year, with U.S. deliveries at 310,000 units. Pent-up demand for IRA-eligible models under the $7,500 tax credit, combined with output from our Nevada Gigafactory expansions, drove U.S. EV market share to 18%. Europe delivered $5.3 billion, or 21%, growing 38% despite softer demand, thanks to the NVX's 520+ mile range and Berlin Gigafactory ramp to 150,000 units annualized. We gained share in Germany and the UK, aided by EU protections on Chinese imports. Asia-Pacific, at 12% or $3 billion, grew 22%, with China deliveries up 15% to 75,000 units via our Shanghai JV, countering BYD and Xiaomi pricing with localized 800V tech and CATL LFP sourcing.

This revenue acceleration stems from supply chain resilience, with in-house 4680 cell production at 80 GWh annualized; product momentum on the NVX platform enabling 20% cost reductions via gigacasting; and software monetization, where our Level 3 autonomy stack boosted recurring revenue to 8% of automotive sales.

Our gross margin was 24.2%, reflecting ongoing operational efficiency. Drilling into gross margin per vehicle, we delivered a record $13,200 per vehicle in Q4, a 22.4% margin on an ASP of $52,800—up sequentially from $12,400 or 21.1% in Q3, and 18% year-over-year from $11,200. Excluding regulatory credits adding $1,800 per vehicle, our core automotive margin highlights manufacturing leverage.

ASP lifted 4% quarter-over-quarter to $52,800 from a mix shift, with premium NVX SUV and NVT pickup at 42% of deliveries. NVT averaged $78,000 ASP with 800V and autonomy stacks. U.S. ASP at $55,200 benefited from IRA rebates; Europe at $48,500 offset competition via CO2 credits; China at $42,000 reflected entry-level tailoring. COGS fell to $39,600 per vehicle, down 7% sequentially and 12% year-over-year. Batteries, 38% of COGS, dropped 16% to $7,200 per kWh-equivalent via 4680 cells powering 65% of output at 280 Wh/kg from Nevada at 100 GWh scaling. Gigacasting cut body-in-white 8%, consolidating parts and reducing waste. LFP stabilization and nickel/cobalt hedges aided.

U.S. COGS at $37,200 for 30% margin; Europe $41,000 improving with Berlin; China $35,500 competitive with locals. Over five quarters, margin per vehicle compounded 15% higher to $13,200 at 85% utilization. Q1 2025 guide: $13,800 at midpoint. Ahead of peers like Tesla's 17.5% core, Rivian's 12-14%. Forward to $16,000 by 2026 via 48V architecture, cell-to-pack, and 95% recycling.

Before segment details, let's cover raw material sourcing and cost management, a key value driver where batteries account for 40-50% of COGS amid 1.2 TWh demand. We've cut COGS per kWh 8% sequentially to $92/kWh, matching Tesla and beating industry $105/kWh average.

Sourcing diversification counters China's 75% cathode dominance and tariffs. Lithium at $15,000/tonne stabilized; nickel $21,000/tonne hedged. Shifted 35% lithium to North America, with Albemarle at Silver Peak for 20 GWh at $12,500/tonne via IRA 45X. Europe Umicore NCM 811 cuts cobalt to under 5%. LFP at $45/kWh in 28% of deliveries shaves $1,200 ASP; high-nickel hedged at $18,500/tonne.

Vertical integration at Nevada Gigafactory 50 GWh captures 15-20% value; $250 million cathode precursor plant at 98% yield cuts to $12/kg. Redwood JV recycled 12,000 tonnes black mass, 95% lithium at $4,000/tonne. Piloting sodium-ion for $60/kWh by 2026. Aluminum/steel contracts reduced non-battery costs 12% to 22% COGS.

Raw materials 42% of $10.5 billion COGS, down from 48%, driving 310bps margin gain. Batteries fell 15% YoY: lithium 28%, nickel 22%, graphite 14%. Hedging 70% H2 shielded rebounds. H2 tailwinds to $85/kWh via LMR cathodes; 45% localized mitigates risks.

Now, on delivery volume guidance by model for Q4 and FY2025. Q4 totaled 485,000 to 505,000 vehicles actually hit midpoint, 22% YoY, 8% sequential from Q3's 465,000, for FY2024 1.92-1.94 million up 28%, margins to 19.5% on FSD 28% take rates. FY2025: 2.35-2.45 million, 22-25% YoY, balanced regions: 45% NA, 35% China/APAC, 20% EMEA.

By model: NV1 Compact (22% Q4 mix), 110,000-115,000 (23% YoY), FY2025 480,000-500,000; 50% China LFP, 30% NA IRA $32k, 20% EMEA RHD. Premium+ FSD 35% take rate, $38k ASP, Shanghai ramp 1,200/week, 380-mile structural packs.

NVX SUV (48% mix), 235,000-245,000 (25% YoY), FY2025 1.15-1.20M; 40% NA, 35% China 7-seater, 25% EMEA. Plaid 12%, $52k ASP, UFC 18-min charge, Texas 2,500/week 4680 20% margins.

NVT Pickup (25% mix), 120,000-125,000 (35% YoY), FY2025 580,000-620,000; 70% NA fleets, 20% Aus/NZ, 10% China. 500+ mile V2G, inventory 2 weeks, NV factory 1,000/week.

NV Van (5% mix), 20,000 units ramping, FY2025 140,000-160,000; 60% China, 30% NA, $65k ASP 800V 450-mile.

Risks: cell shortages, price wars; upsides: EU ban, rebates. Conservative midpoint, $2.5B capex Berlin.

As we wrap Q4 with 52,000 vehicles up 28% and 24.2% margins on core EVs, our strategic outlook for Q1 2025 and FY2025 focuses on scaling production profitability, expanding portfolio with next-gen tech, and deepening regional penetration. North Star: sustainable mobility and shareholder returns.

Pillar 1: Factories at 92% utilization, Nevada and Spartanburg 150,000 run-rate. Q1 production 58,000 units, 12% sequential, $2.8 billion revenue up 32% YoY at $48,000 ASP premium NVX mix.

Initiatives: Battery localization doubles 4680 with Panasonic to 50 GWh, 80% domestic cathode Redwood, 40% less cobalt, IRA tax 15%, 27% Q1 margins. Capex $2.2 billion, 60% automation, $450 million second line, $1.1 billion FCF up from $650 million. Supplier cuts 8% BOM, in-house SiC inverters 5% efficiency.

Prioritizing 18% EBITDA FY2025, 400bps up.

Pillar 2: NVX 65% Q4 deliveries, 520+ mile LFP. Q1 NVX LR Plus 800V, 350 kW 18-min charge, V2G PG&E pilot 5,000 homes.

Pipeline: NVX LR Plus Q1 120,000 units $52k 550-mile L2+ ADAS; NVT Pickup Q2 80,000 $68k 400-mile 14k towing MegaCharger; NV1 Compact Q3 150,000 $34k 300-mile LFP; NVX Autonomy H2 add-on 40% fleet +$8k L4 Waymo.

R&D $850 million, 40% solid-state QuantumScape 800 Wh/kg Q4 20% cost cut NMC. OTA 3.8 mi/kWh, NVIDIA Orin-X 10 million unsupervised miles. 22% CAGR deliveries to 450,000 FY26, 12% U.S. premium share from 8%.

Pillar 3: Premium 25% growth. NA 65% revenue, IRA $7,500, 35% delivery growth, Q1 38,000 U.S., 15,000 stalls NACS 95%. Europe 20%, 50% growth 25,000 units, Berlin Q2 100k dodging duties, 70% localize Euro 7, NVX 15% range edge VW.

China/APAC 10%, Shanghai Q1 12,000 up 40% CATL Qilin, India Q3 Tata 20,000 $30 lakh 30% CAGR. Emerging Brazil/SE Asia LFP.

EV penetration 22% 2025, hedged 70% logistics Red Sea 2-3%. Risks: semis TSMC/Samsung, NHTSA autonomy, Tesla/Rivian—LFP 25% cheaper.

FY2025: $12.5 billion revenue, 27% margins, 15% NA premium share. Operator, back to you after Mike.

Mike Thornton:
Thank you, Sarah. We are pleased with the progress we've made in scaling up production of the NVX. Our Nevada Gigafactory and new Spartanburg site are running at high utilization, with gigacasting and structural battery packs reducing assembly times and costs significantly. We've implemented several initiatives to further improve manufacturing efficiency, including expanding in-house cell production to mitigate supply risks and vertical integration for cathode precursors and recycling. We're on track to meet our production targets for the year, with Q1 sequential growth supporting delivery guidance. Factory output incorporates automation for faster die-casting cycles and higher yields on 4680 cells, positioning us for margin expansion. Berlin Phase 1 comes online Q2, localizing for Europe.

Now, I'll hand the call back to the operator for the Q&A session.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star one on your telephone keypad. To withdraw your question, press star two. Our first question comes from John Mayer with Goldman Sachs.

Analyst 1:
Thanks, good morning. Jordan, with Tesla's Cybertruck ramp and Rivian's R2 launch on the horizon, how do you see NovaVolt maintaining pricing power in the premium pickup and SUV segments?

Jordan Hale:
Good question, John. Our edge is the 25% cheaper LFP stack combined with superior range and fast charging on NVX and NVT. We've held MSRP steady, bundling free lifetime SuperGrid charging on performance trims, defending 22% U.S. midsize EV share. NVT's 500+ mile range and V2G for fleets close gaps quickly, with localized production dodging tariffs.

Operator:
Our next question from Lisa Chen at Morgan Stanley.

Analyst 2:
Sarah, can you expand on the battery cost trajectory into 2025? With lithium stabilizing but nickel volatile, how does hedging impact gross margins?

Sarah Chen:
Absolutely, Lisa. We've hedged 70-80% of exposures, bringing battery packs to $92/kWh now, targeting $85/kWh year-end with LMR trials and recycling yielding 95% lithium recovery. This supports 27% gross margins in Q1, with IRA credits and domestic sourcing boosting effective rates. Vertical integration captures 15-20% more value, ahead of peers.

Operator:
Next from David Kim, Barclays.

Analyst 3:
Mike, on manufacturing, what's the latest on gigafactory expansions and any bottlenecks in scaling 4680 cells?

Mike Thornton:
David, Nevada hits 100 GWh annually by year-end, with second line adding capacity. Spartanburg ramped to 150,000 run-rate; Berlin Q2 at 100k. Bottlenecks minimal—diversified suppliers, gigapress cutting scrap 25%, 40% faster cycles. On track for Q1 58,000 production.

Operator:
From Emily Ross, JPMorgan.

Analyst 4:
Jordan, thoughts on regulatory risks like potential IRA changes or EU tariffs post-elections?

Jordan Hale:
Emily, we're engaged closely with policymakers. IRA localization unlocks full credits; diversified supply chain with 45% North American mitigates. Europe Berlin localizes 70% content for Euro 7. Upside from EU 2035 ban accelerating fleets—guiding conservatively but positioned for tailwinds.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your questions. We have time for one more.

Operator:
Our final question from Tom Patel, Citi.

Analyst 5:
Sarah, FY2025 revenue guide implies strong growth—any color on FCF drivers and capex allocation?

Sarah Chen:
Tom, FY2025 $12.5 billion revenue guide with $1.1 billion FCF from capex discipline at $2.2 billion, 60% to automation and cells. H2 inflection 15% FCF positive, R&D $850 million solid-state and autonomy. Energy storage doubles, software recurring ramps—laser-focused on ROIC over 25%.

Operator:
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Jordan Hale for closing remarks.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders—scaling profitability, innovating our portfolio, and penetrating regions amid EV tailwinds. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the NovaVolt Automotive Q4 2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.

aspect_summary.Raw material sourcing and cost managemen: Battery costs cut 8% to $92/kWh (batteries 38-50% COGS) via diversification (35% NA lithium from Albemarle at $12.5k/tonne, Umicore NCM <5% cobalt, CATL LFP in 28% deliveries), vertical integration (Nevada 50 GWh, $250M cathode plant at $12/kg), Redwood recycling (95% lithium at $4k/tonne), 70% hedging; targeting $85/kWh H2 2025 with LMR cathodes, 45% localization; raw materials down to 42% of COGS.
aspect_summary.Delivery volume guidance by model: FY2025 total: 2.35-2.45M vehicles (+22-25% YoY); NV1 Compact: 480-500k; NVX SUV: 1.15-1.20M; NVT Pickup: 580-620k; NV Van: 140-160k. Q4 2024 actual: 502k total (NV1 ~112.5k, NVX ~240k, NVT ~122.5k, NV Van 20k).
aspect_summary.Gross margin per vehicle: Q4 2024 record $13,200/vehicle (22.4% on $52,800 ASP, excluding $1,800 regulatory credits); up 18% YoY from $11,200; Q1 2025 guide $13,800 midpoint; targeting $16,000 by 2026 via 48V architecture, cell-to-pack, 95% recycling; regional: US $37.2k COGS (30% margin), Europe $41k, China $35.5k.
aspect_summary.Total revenue and year-over-year growth: Q4 2024: $25.3B total (+42% YoY from $17.8B); automotive $22B (+51%, 87% of total), energy storage $2.5B (+28%), services $800M (+35%); FY2025 guide referenced as $12.5B in Q&A (context implies segment or error, primary driver deliveries 2.35-2.45M implying strong growth).
